per_premise.notes: Strong identity via blindfold/hair. Cause (hydraulic hiss) is auditory/off-screen but visual consequence (dust falling) is clear. Good micro-expression.
Clear cause (steam burst). Good use of sleeve flare. Slightly generic 'twist away' but effective.
Balancing on tilting beam is a specific physical constraint. Good silhouette focus.
High energy. Sliding to evade rebar is a clear action. Hair whip adds motion.
Cinematic shot. Crouching under debris is active but slightly passive compared to other dynamic shots. Dust obscuring background risks 'atmospheric filler' if not careful.
Excellent closeup. Wiping fluid is a specific non-weapon hand interaction. Good tension in knuckles.
Leaning back from glass shard. Good counter-rotation description. Distinct from b01_2 steam twist.
Mid-leap. 'Tuck to minimize drag' is a bit technical but works. Hem lift is subtle.
Deflecting crate. Strong impact visual. Dust eruption adds consequence.
Weak. 'Standing directly beneath' is close to static. Looking up with composed focus is a pose rather than an interaction. Sparks dripping are atmospheric.
Heat wave/sweat. Cause is off-screen furnace. Reaction (sweat/jaw clench) is subtle but valid micro-story.
Catching data core. Good weight absorption description. Distinct from other medium shots.
Sliding platform. Similar to b01_3 (tilting/balancing) but different mechanism (sliding vs balancing). Acceptable variation.
Swinging chain. High motion blur potential. Clear cause (debris wave).
Turbine blade. Crouched defensive stance is similar to b01_5 (crouching under threat). 'Eyes tracking' helps but still feels like a pose.
Cable snap. Good micro-expression of pain/stoicism. Distinct from other closeups.
Pressing control panel. Hair lifting from static is a nice detail. Distinct interaction.
Slipping on glass. S-curve twist is dynamic. Good use of stockings reveal.
Wind shear skidding. High energy. Similar to b01_2 (wind/steam force) but different body reaction (skid vs twist).
Chimney edge. Balancing/leaning back is similar to b01_3 and b03_3 (balancing on unstable surface). Repetition of 'balance' hook.

strengths: Strong adherence to character identity facts (blindfold, hair, dress details) across all premises.
Most dynamic and full-body shots have clear causal triggers (rebar, crate, wind shear).
Closeups successfully avoid the 'gripping sword' trap with varied hand/face interactions.
failures: Repetition of 'balancing on unstable surface' hook in Fullbody category (b01_3, b03_3, b04_5).
Cinematic shots (b02_5, b03_5) lean towards static poses ('standing beneath', 'crouched defensive') rather than active environmental interaction.
Some medium shots rely heavily on 'twist/lean' as the primary verb, reducing variety in upper-body dynamics.
desired_patterns: Integration of clothing physics (sleeve flare, hem lift) with specific forces.
Micro-expressions that reflect stoic personality under stress.
undesired_patterns: Static balancing poses without immediate threat progression.
Atmospheric elements (dust, sparks) serving as the only visual interest in cinematic shots.
Generic 'looking up' or 'crouching' without specific physical interaction with the environment.
recommendations_for_next_cycle: Replace one 'balancing' fullbody shot with a different physical constraint (e.g., climbing, hanging from a hook, crawling under low clearance).
Make cinematic shots more active: instead of standing/crouching, have the character interacting with the environment (pushing against a closing door, pulling a lever to stop a machine).
Vary medium shot verbs beyond 'twist/lean': include reaching, pushing, pulling, or catching.
verdict: Good batch with strong identity and visual appeal. Main weakness is repetition in the Fullbody category (balancing) and slightly passive Cinematic shots. Needs minor adjustments to break the balancing cluster and add more active environmental interaction in wide shots.
